blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: National Income Concepts are crucial for understanding macroeconomic growth and output.
Union Budget Concepts detail the financial allocations, revenues, and expenditure of the Central Government.
Taxation in India is bifurcated into Direct Taxes and Indirect Taxes.
Economic planning in India transitioned from traditional Five Year Plans to NITI Aayog.

cells: Total value of goods/services produced within country's borders
GDP adjusted for inflation using base year prices
Revenue receipts (taxes, non-tax) and revenue expenditure (salaries, subsidies, interest)
Capital receipts (borrowings, disinvestment) and capital expenditure (assets, loans given)
Total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings; indicator of govt borrowing need
Revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts; reflects current account imbalance
Fiscal Deficit minus interest payments; reflects current year borrowing needs
Revenue Deficit minus grants for capital asset creation (GFCE)
Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act; mandates reduction in fiscal deficit
Main fund; all revenue/capital receipts; all expenditure drawn from here
Rs.500 crore; for unforeseen expenditure; Parliament approval later
For funds where govt acts as banker; provident funds, small savings, etc.

rows: Levied directly on the income, profit, or wealth of an individual or entity.
Levied on goods and services rather than on income or profits.
The tax burden cannot be shifted to another person.
The tax burden can be shifted from the seller to the ultimate consumer.

items: Income Tax – levied on individual/corporate income; administered by CBDT
Corporate Tax – on company profits; reduced to 22% for domestic companies (15% for new manufacturing)
Capital Gains Tax – on profit from sale of capital assets; STCG and LTCG
Securities Transaction Tax (STT) – on equity trading; collected at GBOurce
GST (Goods and Services Tax) – introduced July 1, 2017; replaced VAT, Service Tax, Excise
Customs Duty – on import/export of goods; administered by CBIC
GST Council – chaired by Union Finance Minister; 2/3 weightage to states, 1/3 to Centre

cells: Essential food items, fresh produce, education, healthcare
Basic necessities, packaged food, economy class air travel
Luxury goods, sin goods (tobacco, aerated drinks), automobiles

items: Questions frequently distinguish between Direct Taxes and Indirect Taxes in terms of incidence and impact.
Key differences between the former Planning Commission's Five Year Plans and NITI Aayog's bottom-up approach are vital for civil services exams.
National Income aggregates (GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP) and fiscal deficit terms from Union Budgets are high-yield topics.

blocks.content: India's Planning Commission (est. 1950) oversaw twelve Five Year Plans. It was replaced by NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) on January 1, 2015.

items: NITI Aayog is a policy think tank; does not allocate funds (unlike Planning Commission)
Headed by Prime Minister; CEO is key executive official
Key documents: India@2047 Vision, National Development Agenda
